Default load initializes text NULL, uses fopen rt, seeks/ftell and casts unsigned size without explicit return checks; size zero does not allocate. fopen failure/nonpositive unsigned size path returns initial NULL if logging completes.

Default positive-size load allocates size+1 zeroed chars; after nonnull allocation reads count, reassigns RL_REALLOC result when count<size, then writes text[count]=zero with no explicit realloc-null guard. No universal allocation-failure safety guarantee.

Default opened-file normal path calls fclose without checking return; UnloadFileText simply delegates RL_FREE(text). A custom callback allocation must be compatible with the caller release scheme; selected code does not enforce allocator compatibility.

fprintf negative return selects warning but does not gate later result=true; fclose()==0 alone sets true in shown default path, assuming earlier operations return. Therefore true is not a written conjunction of nonnegative fprintf and successful fclose, nor durability proof.

Text callback setters assign shared static function pointers, without visible synchronization or lifetime/return validation. NULL assignment follows same setter body, restoring default dispatch for subsequent nonnull filename calls.
